references.note: Where the problem is listed; the registry's own reference.
references.title: Singmaster's conjecture (Wikipedia)

references.note: Poses the problem and proves N(t) = O(log t).
references.title: D. Singmaster, How often does an integer occur as a binomial coefficient?, Amer. Math. Monthly 78 (1971), 385-386

references.note: N(t) = O(log t / log log t).
references.title: H. L. Abbott, P. Erdős and D. Hanson, On the number of times an integer occurs as a binomial coefficient, Amer. Math. Monthly 81 (1974), 256-261

references.note: Best general bound I know of, N(t) = O(log t · log log log t / (log log t)^3).
references.title: D. M. Kane, Improved bounds on the number of ways of expressing t as a binomial coefficient, Integers 7 (2007)

references.note: For t large, at most a bounded number of solutions with k in the interior range exp((log n)^(2/3+ε)) ≤ k ≤ n/2; the small-k range remains open.
references.title: K. Matomäki, M. Radziwiłł, X. Shao, T. Tao and J. Teräväinen, Singmaster's conjecture in the interior of Pascal's triangle (2021)

literature_proposed.summary: Open. Best known general bounds grow with t (Singmaster 1971, Abbott–Erdős–Hanson 1974, Kane 2007); a bounded count is known only for solutions deep in the interior of the triangle (Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Shao–Tao–Teräväinen 2021). The value 3003 occurs eight times, the most known. References recalled from memory by the filer and not re-checked against the papers in this session; bibliographic details should be verified by a steward.

justification.text: `t > 1` is Singmaster's own range: the informal text says 'any number t > 1', excluding t = 1, which appears infinitely often on the border of Pascal's triangle; the boundary is the stated one.
